operations.name: get_health
operations.description: Bridge, terminal and broker-connection state; polling latencies. Call this first: it tells whether the terminal is connected to the broker.

operations.name: get_terminal
operations.description: Build, broker, server, algo-trading enabled, observed time contract.

operations.name: get_account
operations.description: Balance, equity, margin, position-accounting mode, currency.

operations.name: list_symbols
operations.description: Available symbols.

operations.name: get_symbol
operations.description: Tick size, step, min/max volume, filling modes, sessions, trading status. Read this before building an order: prices must be multiples of tick_size and volumes multiples of volume_step within volume_min and volume_max.

operations.name: get_bars
operations.description: Closed bars of a date range, one page at a time. The closed bars with from_epoch <= time < to_epoch, read in pages. Bars are asked for by date range and timeframe, never by quantity. The range is cut into time windows of 1000 bar lengths, so total_pages follows from the dates and the timeframe alone and is the same on every page: read page 1, then every page up to total_pages (or follow next_page until it is null). A page holds the bars that exist in its window, oldest first: over a weekend or a holiday it is empty, and that is not the end of the range. Bars older than the terminal's own history ("Max. bars in chart") are absent, not an error.

from_epoch.description: Start of the range, inclusive, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

to_epoch.description: End of the range, exclusive, in seconds since the Unix epoch.

page.description: The page to read, from 1 to total_pages.

operations.name: get_latest_tick
operations.description: The terminal's current quote for one symbol. The terminal's current tick (symbol_info_tick) as a zero- or one-element array: what a stream client reloads after a gap on the ticks channel. Empty when the terminal has no quote for the symbol.

operations.name: get_ticks
operations.description: Ticks of a date range, one page at a time. The ticks with from_time_msc <= time_msc < to_time_msc, oldest first, read in pages of at most 1000 ticks. Ticks are asked for by date range, never by quantity. The number of ticks in a period is not known before reading them, so there is no page count: send the first request without cursor, then repeat it with the next_cursor of each answer until next_cursor is null. A page can hold fewer than 1000 ticks, or none, and still have a next_cursor. Keep symbol, from_time_msc and to_time_msc the same for every page of one range.

from_time_msc.description: Start of the range, inclusive, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

to_time_msc.description: End of the range, exclusive, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

cursor.description: The next_cursor of the previous page; omit it for the first page.

operations.name: get_book

operations.name: list_open_orders
operations.description: Open orders (bridge journal view). This is the bridge's own journal; an order sent outside the bridge is not here.

operations.name: submit_order
operations.description: Submit order — idempotent by client_order_id. Sends a real order to the broker account. Choose a fresh, unique client_order_id; repeating the call with the same id and the same payload returns the first order and never sends a second one. A state of UNKNOWN means the bridge could not confirm the outcome: do not resubmit under a new id, read the order with get_order and tell the operator. price is required for LIMIT, STOP and STOP_LIMIT orders.

operations.description: Cancel. The returned state can be FILLED when the cancellation lost the race.

operations.name: replace_order
operations.description: Explicit cancel-replace with operation_id and new_client_order_id. Idempotent by operation_id: repeating the same request returns the stored outcome; a different payload under the same operation_id is a conflict (mirrors client_order_id idempotency). Choose a fresh operation_id; repeating the call with the same operation_id returns the stored outcome. Read the outcome field: both orders can end open, or neither.

operations.name: reconcile_order
operations.description: Re-examine one UNKNOWN order against the terminal. Audited. A known ticket takes the terminal's state; an entry without a ticket resolves to a unique magic+tag candidate, or to REJECTED only when the terminal holds no order or deal with this bridge's magic in a window covering the entry. Anything else stays UNKNOWN and keeps its symbol blocked. For an operator resolving an order stuck in UNKNOWN.

operations.name: list_history_orders
operations.description: from_epoch and to_epoch bound the search window.

operations.name: list_history_deals
operations.description: from_epoch and to_epoch bound the search window.

operations.name: activate_kill_switch
operations.description: {action: HALT_NEW_ORDERS | CANCEL_ALL | FLATTEN} Emergency stop, and it only escalates: HALT_NEW_ORDERS blocks new orders, CANCEL_ALL also cancels every open order, FLATTEN also closes every position at market. Only rearm_kill_switch returns it to NORMAL.

operations.name: rearm_kill_switch
operations.description: Rearm — return the kill switch to NORMAL. Orders are accepted again afterwards. An operator's decision: do not call it unless the user asked for exactly this.

operations.name: heartbeat
operations.description: Feed the dead-man switch. Every call (re)establishes the lease. Once a lease exists and no heartbeat arrives within the timeout, the bridge cancels all open orders. The first heartbeat arms the dead-man switch: from then on, open orders are canceled when heartbeats stop for longer than the bridge's timeout. Do not call it unless you will keep calling it.
